```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = FALSE,
  comment = "",
  class.output = "spax-output"
)
```

The guides use the bundled Cornwall GP data, described in [The Cornwall GP
example data](cornwall-data.html); this page needs no data.

```{r packages}
library(spax)
```

Function names follow one rule: the prefix says what a function is for, and
the suffix names the thing.

- `spax()` and `spax_<model>()` run an analysis. `spax()` runs a model
  specification on prepared data; `spax_huff()` and `spax_clm()` run the Huff
  model and the conditional logit from raw inputs; `spax_2sfca()`,
  `spax_e2sfca()` and the other FCA functions compute an FCA index.
- `prep_` prepares data: `prep_data()`.
- `spec_` specifies a model without data: `spec_huff()`, `spec_clm()`.
- `decay_` declares a decay kernel: `decay_gaussian()`, `decay_exponential()`,
  `decay_power()`, `decay_custom()` and `decay_kernel()`.
- `obs_` declares observations: `obs_flows()`, `obs_totals()`.
- `calc_`, `gather_` and `spread_` are the building blocks.

A model keeps its name as the suffix: `spax_huff()` runs the Huff model and
`spec_huff()` specifies it. The earlier allocation names stay: the model
declarations `clm_allocation()` and `huff_allocation()` and the steps
`<verb>_allocation()`, such as `fit_allocation()`, which `spax()` uses
underneath. The allocation functions are experimental. Existing FCA calls and
result types remain supported.

## Choose the level of operation

| Task | Public interface | What it returns |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Binary catchment FCA | `spax_2sfca()` | `spax` result with accessibility raster |
| Distance-weighted FCA | `spax_e2sfca()` | `spax` result with accessibility raster |
| Squared access-side decay FCA | `spax_m2sfca()` | `spax` result with accessibility raster |
| Selection-weighted FCA | `spax_3sfca()`, `spax_huff2sfca()` | `spax` result with accessibility raster |
| Supply/demand calculation using supplied kernels | `compute_access()` | Accessibility `SpatRaster` |
| Decay, normalization or choice weights | `calc_decay()`, `decay_kernel()`, `calc_normalize()`, `calc_choice()` | See the individual input/output contracts |
| Weighted reduction to facilities | `gather_weighted()`, `gather_demand()` | Facility vector/table |
| Weighted distribution to origins | `spread_weighted()`, `spread_access()` | Raster result |
| Run an allocation model in one call | `spax()`, `spax_huff()`, `spax_clm()` | Experimental allocation result (`spax_allocation`) |
| Prepare allocation data | `prep_data()` | Prepared inputs |
| Specify an allocation model without data | `spec_huff()`, `spec_clm()` with `decay_gaussian()`, `decay_exponential()`, `decay_power()` or `decay_custom()` | Model specification (`spax_spec`) |
| Declare observed counts | `obs_flows()`, `obs_totals()` | Observations and their loss (`spax_obs`) |
| Allocation steps: prepare and declare | `prepare_allocation()`, `clm_allocation()`, `huff_allocation()` | Prepared inputs and experimental model |
| Allocation steps: fit, evaluate, predict and bootstrap | `fit_allocation()`, `evaluate_allocation()`, `predict_allocation()`, `bootstrap_allocation()` | Model-specific saved results |
| Check and compare fitted allocations | `check_allocation()`, `compare_allocations()` | Comparison tables; the fits are not changed |
| Travel times and demand inputs | `calc_travel_time()`, `calc_demand()` | Travel matrix or raster; demand raster or vector |

These function families share concepts such as supply, demand and facility IDs.
Their arguments and result meanings are not interchangeable. In particular,
`calc_normalize()` applied to a numeric matrix normalizes the whole matrix,
whereas a multilayer raster is normalized across layers at each cell. Select the
operation appropriate to the declared axes; do not infer behavior from a name.

```{r public-interface-check}
functions <- c(
  # FCA accessibility
  "spax_2sfca", "spax_e2sfca", "spax_m2sfca", "spax_3sfca", "spax_huff2sfca",
  "compute_access",
  # Allocation interface (experimental)
  "spax", "spax_huff", "spax_clm", "prep_data", "spec_huff", "spec_clm",
  "decay_gaussian", "decay_exponential", "decay_power", "decay_custom",
  "obs_flows", "obs_totals",
  # Allocation steps (experimental)
  "prepare_allocation", "clm_allocation", "huff_allocation", "fit_allocation",
  "evaluate_allocation", "predict_allocation", "bootstrap_allocation",
  "check_allocation", "compare_allocations",
  # Input helpers
  "calc_travel_time", "calc_demand", "decay_kernel"
)

# Every name above is exported by the installed package
stopifnot(all(functions %in% getNamespaceExports("spax")))
data.frame(function_name = functions)
```

The former iterative-FCA interface is no longer available. It is not an alias
for static CLM or a supported fixed-point workflow. Private functions beginning
with `.` and other unexported implementation functions are not public contracts;
examples for users should not call them with `:::`.

## Inspect saved results using standard R generics

| Result | Inspection | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|:--|
| FCA `spax` object | `print()`, `summary()`, `plot()`, `$accessibility` | Saved supply-per-demand index; raster-cell summary |
| Allocation result of `spax()` | `coef()`, `fitted()`, `summary()`, `as.data.frame()` with `type` `"parameters"`, `"facilities"`, `"origins"`, `"flows"` or `"starts"`, `predict()` | The bound model with its fit or evaluation; an output that was not saved is computed when asked for |
| Allocation multistart fit | `coef()`, `fitted()`, `summary()`, `as.data.frame(type = "parameters")`, `plot()` | Selected fit plus retained per-start diagnostics |
| Allocation coverage | `summary()`, `as.data.frame(type = "regional")` or `type = "cells"` | Saved coverage on retained positive-demand support |
| Allocation bootstrap | `summary()`, `as.data.frame(type = "estimates")`, `"draws"`, `"starts"`, `plot()` | Saved point/interval status and every attempted result |

Inspection does not refit the allocation model or resample the bootstrap. A
failed search can still be summarized, but parameter extraction requires an
eligible selected fit. Bootstrap methods preserve incomplete and refused
statuses; displaying a point estimate does not make an interval available.

FCA rasters and allocation numeric tables have different storage contracts. Use
`terra::as.data.frame()` to extract raster cell values, and preserve geometry
separately. Allocation tables carry IDs; coverage tables also carry unit,
support and reporting attributes. CSV loses those attributes, so retain the
documented RDS bundle when exporting allocation results.

## Keep input validation enabled

Some legacy functions expose `snap`. Leave its default `FALSE` in ordinary user
code. It is an internal optimization switch, not a different model or a general
speed recommendation. New prepared allocation inputs validate IDs, geometry and
support at their own boundary and do not use a universal `snap` convention.

See [Choosing an FCA index or an allocation model](model-choice.html) for a
runnable comparison, [The E2SFCA calculation step by step](e2sfca-steps.html)
for public building blocks, the [allocation workflow](allocation-workflow.html)
for fitting, prediction, scenarios and persistence, and [Bootstrap intervals
for a fitted allocation model](facility-bootstrap.html) for intervals.
